evidence.description: The 'shared' property is a static variable on a struct, which is not thread-safe and can lead to race conditions when accessed or modified from multiple threads.

candidates.explanation: The 'User' type is a struct, but it exposes a static 'shared' property. In Swift, structs are value types, and static properties on structs are shared across all instances. Accessing and modifying 'shared' from different threads simultaneously can cause data races, especially since the 'didSet' observer performs asynchronous tasks and file I/O.
candidates.title: Thread Safety Issue with Static Shared Property

evidence.description: The 'save' method uses 'Task.detached' to perform file I/O, but it captures 'self' (a struct) which is then encoded. This can lead to inconsistent states if the struct is modified between the time 'save' is called and the task executes.

candidates.explanation: Because 'User' is a struct, 'let user = self' creates a local copy. If the 'shared' instance is updated immediately after 'save()' is called but before the detached task executes, the file will be saved with stale data. Furthermore, 'Task.detached' does not guarantee execution order.
candidates.title: Potential Data Inconsistency in Asynchronous Save

evidence.description: The 'init(from decoder: Decoder)' method uses 'try?' for almost every property, which suppresses decoding errors and defaults to initial values without notifying the caller of corrupted or missing data.

candidates.explanation: Using 'try?' inside a custom 'init(from:)' is an anti-pattern for 'Codable'. It prevents the decoder from throwing errors when the underlying data is malformed, potentially leading to the application running with incorrect or partially loaded configuration data without any error reporting.
candidates.title: Silent Decoding Failures

evidence.description: The 'stored' property performs a file read and JSON decoding every time it is accessed, which is inefficient.

candidates.explanation: The 'stored' computed property performs disk I/O and JSON decoding on every access. Since 'init()' calls this property to populate the struct, it is functional, but if 'stored' were accessed elsewhere, it would cause significant performance degradation.
candidates.title: Inefficient Disk I/O in Computed Property
